findings.source_passage: whose plumage-like, tufted droopings seemed his verdant jet
findings.source_locator: paragraph 6, describing the stranded whale with head against a cocoa-nut tree
findings.why_it_matters: This poetic simile connecting the palm tree's fronds to the whale's spout is a small but characteristically Melvillean image — it anticipates the weaver-loom passage by merging natural and cetacean imagery. Its loss flattens the visual transition into the great symbolic passage that follows.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'with his head against a cocoa-nut tree, whose plumage-like, tufted droopings seemed his verdant jet' in the stranded-whale description.

findings.source_passage: King Tranquo seizing his because he wanted it; and Sir Clifford, because he was lord of the seignories of those parts
findings.source_locator: second-to-last substantial paragraph, on proprietorial claims
findings.why_it_matters: This dry, satirical aside on the legal/regal logic of ownership is a quintessential Melvillean ironic observation — raw power (Tranquo) vs. feudal right (Sir Clifford) collapsed into comic equivalence. It carries interpretive weight on themes of ownership and authority, and its removal erases the satirical bite.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the sentence contrasting the two proprietorial claims verbatim or near-verbatim: 'King Tranquo seizing his because he wanted it; and Sir Clifford, because he was lord of the seignories of those parts.'

findings.source_passage: threepence to hear the echo in the hollow of his cerebellum
findings.source_locator: Sir Clifford paragraph, admission prices list
findings.why_it_matters: The draft includes twopence and sixpence but omits the middle item (threepence for the cerebellum echo), truncating the comic escalating list of admission charges. The rhythm of the three-part joke is broken.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'threepence to hear the echo in the hollow of his cerebellum' between the twopence and sixpence items.

summary: The draft preserves all high-priority material including the full weaver-god passage and Life/Death paragraph verbatim, but loses two minor-to-medium voice moments — the satirical ownership contrast and the middle item in Sir Clifford's comic admission-price list — plus a small but characteristically Melvillean image of the palm's 'verdant jet.'
